(1) the CCR ratio model can be used to estimate both technical and scale efficiency, and (2) the CCR multiplier model can be used for estimating only the technical inefficiency.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of mathematical programming to evaluate management accomplishments.
the identification of sources of inefficiencies, the magnitudes of such inefficiencies, and their correction.

the development and use of new mathematical programming techniques which can be used to evaluate the efficiency of the management of organizations and which are based on a new ratio form which is directly applicable to observed data without requiring a specification of weights or functional forms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Data Envelopment Analysis provides a general mathematical programming approach for identifying and correcting technical inefficiencies in multiple input, multiple output situations.
the new model is a natural extension of the CCR model which provides a more complete and detailed analysis of the efficiency of a firm's operation.

the new model developed in this paper is an improvement over the earlier models of Charnes, et al., in that it provides for a more complete analysis and a more comprehensive evaluation of the relative efficiencies and the sources of inefficiencies in multiple input and output cases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the methods of Data Envelopment Analysis are extended to provide not only a separation of technical from scale inefficiencies but also an explicit determination of the type of scale inefficiency present.

the present methods make it possible to identify and correct for technical inefficiencies and to determine whether operations have been conducted in regions of decreasing, constant or increasing returns to scale.
the present paper extends the CCR ratio form to include a new variable which permits identification of returns to scale.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CCR ratio form of DEA can be extended to include a new variable which makes it possible for managers to identify the nature of returns to scale in a given situation.
Data Envelopment Analysis is capable of providing a comprehensive and integrated approach to management evaluation and planning.
DEA is a very useful tool for management and policy makers.
